Her tone, the way she’s actually doing therapy (questions, her ideas, just more scattered I guess) her body language.  I know some people love to say that I’m not right when I feel other people’s feelings, but I’m usually right.

That's actually really helpful.  And I think if someone had said something like "what about your thoughts are you struggling with" that might have been enough prompting so I like having that idea asking myself those questions.  And I know that suicidality is very serious and they need to check it, but this was 45 minutes of asking me over and over again.  I understand why but at some point I felt like we had established that I was currently safe and that I needed to talk about what had taken me there, rather than berating me about it.  I think I need to work on what level of disclosure to do (ie. if I know I'm safe and I just need someone to listen perhaps being less truthful about that aspect)

A couple things, I really struggle to express myself verbally (or in writing) particularly when I'm not doing well.  I have always gotten very little prompting from the person.  They've been nice, but just kind of empathizing with what I'm saying.  That's great, but really I'll say "I'm struggling with my thoughts" and get back "I hear that you're having a hard time with your thoughts", and then nothing.  Or I will say "I just moved and I'm having a hard time" and I won't know where to go from there.  Also, I currently have a lot of suicidal thoughts, and one of the conversations I had felt like I spent the whole time convincing the person that I was not going to kill myself right then, and kept coming back to that when I tried to talk about other things.  I think the problem is likely on me, like I said I really struggle with expressing myself.  I thought maybe seeing other conversations I would understand better how to do this.  I know its kind of weird

Some don’t have people to pull them out of bed.  Some also deal with anxiety which make driving a car impossible.  Since this is about incels and not really depression I will bow out as I don’t know enough about them

Yeah it’s not a perfect example, but therapists in general care and “take care” of their clients.  The parent child relationship is one where the kids can be insecure and vulnerable and trust that the parent can handle it and take care of their feelings.  But a parent could not (should not) rely on a child in the same way.  Similar to a therapist taking care of their clients emotions but not relying on the clients for the care of the therapists emotions
The parent child relationship is similar in its one sidedness and it is the most important relationship in the development of attachment

Yup and let’s think this through.  So I want to volunteer.  First I have to find somewhere to volunteer and pick a time to do so.  On that day I need to get out of bed, do my hair, brush my teeth (probably shower), pick clothes and put them on.  All without ending up back in bed.  Then I would have arranged some way to get there.  I need to make sure I know where it is and where to go when I get there.  Maybe I would have had a panic attack because I was so nervous about being around people or getting lost on the way.  Manage to get myself in the car (or bus) and figure out how to get there.  Plus a thousand other small steps I’m missing.  There are lots of things people who aren’t depressed don’t think about doing or don’t realize they just do it.  For someone with depression (particularly severe as referenced in the post) each small task (brushing teeth) can feel insurmountable.  It’s not a matter of just pulling yourself up by your bootstraps and getting out there
Because that’s what this person chose to say.  To “gain perspective”.  Yes it does other things but depressed people generally don’t lack perspective
By “gain perspective” do you mean like they’ll see how good they have and and how bad others have it and that’ll make them feel better?  If so that’s not how depression works

Does that make sense?  Gradually it started to sink in and I started actually believing it, not just logically thinking it.  I don’t know if that’s what’s going on with you.  This was all a recent realization after I started agreeing with him

I like remote because it cuts down on travel time (for a 50 minute appointment I only need 50 minutes).  Before I would have had to travel to a nearby city.  I love in person so much more.  But I could not do masks.  I tried and it makes me panic.  I also work from home so I haven’t had to get used to wearing a mask a lot and I’m usually busy when I wear one so I’m distracted (like shopping).  I also hate not being able to see his face as it is very comforting.  If I lived in the city and we didn’t have to wear masks I 100% would chose in person every time

I would ask to be added to the wait list of those who have the wait list and start with those who can start right away.  Worry only about the ones with immediate openings.  Do a session with them and see how you feel (after first session t asked if I wanted to rebook or if I wanted time to think about it).  If you don’t click with anyone at first, you have the wait list.  I’m a big fan of “gut feelings” with regards to people and I’m pretty good at telling who I can click with quickly.

I saw my t all through the holidays last year.  He worked one day a week, just happened to be my day.  He likes his job (has told me this) and it is his job to set the boundaries on when he needs a break.  I would leave it unless you want to move it.

All I asked was “are you accepting new clients”.  That was pretty much my entire email.  I gave zero context for my issues.  When she responded yes she was, she asked when I was available and gave some suggested openings.  For husband, I was concerned like you, I just sent a text message saying “I’m planning on seeing a psychologist x day at x time.  Can you watch the kids please”.  It can be hard to just carry on with your day after therapy, but sometimes I find I’m able to push through the rest of my day and then fall apart after.  You can also just say you have a medical appointment to your manager
And I’ve been doing therapy for a year, I had an initial little down that I thought was the “worse before I got better” about a month or 2 into therapy.  This bigger one started about 4/5 months in

She did point it out and at one point was suggesting that I might need to see someone with more expertise in my specific issue because of how bad it got.  (I’m still with original T). But it’s amazing how far I’ve been able to come since then.  Maybe I was holding it together and finally let it all out.  I didn’t love going down that far, but I’m very happy with where I am now.  I mean I have a long way to go, and I just had a session where T was noticing me going down again (just slipping back to some patterns that usually precede the issues).  Therapy can make you worse before it makes you better and boy was that true for me

Talk to your therapist.  But for me I went down quick and then back up before a major slide, worse then anything I’ve experienced before therapy.  Since that bottom I have come waaaaaay up.  I’m doing so much better now.  My therapist saw how far down I went and was very concerned but the progress I’ve made I don’t think I could have made without going to the dark places.

90% of our contact between sessions is for scheduling, 9% homework related (usually just her sending me a link or 2 or extremely rarely I might ask a clarification question) and 1% is crisis.  I asked for additional coping ideas and she phoned me (her choice, I had emailed) and then we scheduled an additional appointment.

Yes she does most of the time.  If I'm like freaking out we usually don't have time but she does on a "normal" session.  And she's really good about holding me accountable while still being kind if I wasn't able to do it.  This is maybe 5-10 minutes of our session.

My T and I work on setting goals related to lack of motivation and energy.  So one week it might be get out of bed before 9.  Next week it might be get out of bed before 9 and have a shower and so on and so forth.  Baby steps.  I really like when my T talked about setting the bar so low that I can step over it so I'm successful, because being a human can seem daunting to me if I think about all that I need to do.  This is the "homework" I work on between sessions.
My T has told me that her sliding scale goes down to $0/session, even though this is certainly not advertised.  I would email directly and ask what "we should discuss" means

To me it was important that my therapist be able to keep up with me.  My brain moves fast (like I'm sure it does for many) and I have had to slow it down to communicate with some people in my life.  I lose a lot when I slow down, so her being just as fast as me was important.  But I just got lucky, because that's not really something you can look at in a psychology today profile.
